subject: runaway freight locomotive
title: What If a Freight Train Ran Away With Nobody Aboard? Ohio, 2001

scenes.text: What if a loaded freight train ran away with nobody aboard? In 2001, one did. Carrying poison.
scenes.keywords: freight locomotive rail yard tank car

scenes.text: May 15th, 2001, Ohio. An engineer stepped off to throw a switch, leaving locomotive 8888 in full throttle, not brake.
scenes.keywords: track switch lever locomotive cab throttle

scenes.text: Forty-seven cars rolled south with no one aboard, two tankers of molten phenol, hitting 51 miles an hour.
A derailer was flung off the track. Police fired shotguns at the fuel cutoff button and hit the fuel cap instead.
Sixty-six miles later, engineer Jess Knowlton chased it down in another locomotive, coupled to the last car and braked hard.
At eleven miles an hour, trainmaster Jon Hosfeld ran alongside, jumped aboard and killed the throttle. Hollywood called it Unstoppable.
scenes.keywords: man running beside train cab ladder

description:
What if a freight train ran away with nobody aboard? On 15 May 2001, CSX locomotive 8888 left a yard near Toledo, Ohio, under full power with 47 cars, two of them tankers of molten phenol, and ran unmanned for about 66 miles at up to 51 to 53 mph.
A derailer failed and police shotgun fire missed the fuel cutoff. A chasing locomotive crew coupled to the rear and slowed it, and trainmaster Jon Hosfeld boarded at about 11 mph and shut it down. The 2010 film Unstoppable was based on it.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The fuel cutoff button had to be held down for several seconds, so even a perfect shot would not have stopped it. How would you have stopped the train? And what should we run through next?
